newsitem.title: GERMANY: Govt still ready to talk with SPD on tax - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Govt still ready to talk with SPD on tax - Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday the government was still ready to talk with the main opposition Social Democrats (SPD) about tax reforms despite the SPD's decision to postpone the talks.

"We are open for further talks but there must be a real will on the part of the SPD to reach an agreement," Waigel said in a statement after the SPD postponed talks set for Saturday in protest of government plans to cut aid to coal miners.
"Cancellation of the talks by the SPD is completely unjustified and helps neither the miners nor Germany's unemployed," Waigel said further.

Waigel said the SPD appeared to be using the dispute with the miners as a ploy to back out of the talks that are aimed reaching a bipartisan compromise on tax reforms that could provide a net tax cut of around 30 billion marks.

The third round of talks between Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition and the SPD had been set for Saturday, but the SPD baulked in protest at a government proposal to cut aid to miners to 3.8 billion marks from the year 2005. It currently provides around 10 billion marks a year.
"There was and is no connection between planned tax reforms and talks about coal subsidies," Waigel said.
